title: Whooper settings
description: The settings in Whooper's config.toml that a settings form may edit. bin/whooper-settings prints and saves them.

schedule.title: Polling
schedule.description: When bin/whooper-run polls: a round starts the interval after the last one ended, at or after the start and before the end, on the chosen days.

interval_minutes.title: Poll every (minutes)
interval_minutes.description: Minutes from the end of one round to the start of the next. Each poll runs a model.

start.title: Start
start.description: The local time of day rounds start from, as a 24-hour time such as 10:00.

end.title: End
end.description: The local time of day from which no round starts, such as 18:00. It must be after the start; a round that starts before it may finish after it.

notify.title: Notification script
notify.description: A script whooper-round runs as <script> <title> <message> when a review finishes or fails, such as one that shows a macOS notification. Relative to the config file's folder.

timeout_minutes.title: Stop a poll after (minutes)
timeout_minutes.description: whooper-poll stops a poll run that runs longer, and the next poll reads the same posts again. At least 5: a poll takes 2 to 3 minutes.

jobs.title: Agents
jobs.description: The agent each job runs on. agents/ has a folder per agent with a launcher per job it can run.

poll.title: Poll agent
poll.description: Reads the ask channel's posts and picks the review asks.

agents.title: Models
agents.description: Each agent's models. Model names are the agent's own: Devin's names add the effort level.

timeout_minutes.title: Stop a review after (minutes)
timeout_minutes.description: whooper-review stops a review that runs longer, and counts it as a failure.

skills.title: Review skills
skills.description: The skills each review run loads, by folder name in ~/.claude/skills.

timeout_minutes.title: Stop an answer after (minutes)
timeout_minutes.description: whooper-ask stops a run that takes longer to answer a question about a review, and saves no answer. Any number above 0, such as 2.5.
